chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi narrated to us from Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who narrated from Abdullah ibn Kharash, who narrated from Ahmad ibn Bard, who narrated from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them, from Abu Lababah ibn Abd al-Mundhir,

that he went to collect a debt from Abu al-Yasar that was owed to him. He heard him say: "Tell him he is not here." So Abu Lababah called out: "O Abu al-Yasar, come out to me!" He came out to him. Abu Lababah asked: "What made you do this?" He said: "Hardship, O Abu Lababah." He asked: "Do you swear by God?" He said: "By God."

Then Abu Lababah said: "I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, say: 'Who would like to be sheltered from the outburst of hellfire?' We said: 'All of us would like that, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Then let him give respite to his debtor, or let him forgive the one in hardship.'"

key_terms.العسر: Hardship, financial difficulty, inability to repay a debt
key_terms.المعسر: The one in financial hardship, unable to pay debts
key_terms.غريم: Debtor or creditor; here meaning the person who owes a debt
key_terms.فور جهنم: The outburst or intense heat of hellfire
key_terms.يستظل: To seek shade or shelter; metaphor for divine protection

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving respite to a debtor in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident where Abu Lababah came to collect a debt from Abu al-Yasar, who was hiding due to financial hardship. When Abu al-Yasar confirmed his difficulty on oath, Abu Lababah cited a prophetic tradition that whoever gives respite to a debtor or forgives one in hardship will be sheltered from the heat of hellfire. This teaching, delivered by the Prophet (SAWW) to his companions in Medina, emphasized the virtue of leniency toward debtors as a means of gaining divine protection.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi, reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who reported from Abdullah ibn Kharash, who reported from Ahmad ibn Bard, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father, Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon them, from Lababah ibn Abd al-Munzar,

that he went to collect his debt from Abu al-Yasar. He heard him say: "Tell him, he is not here." So Abu Lababah exclaimed: "O Abu Yasar, come out." He came out. Abu Lababah asked: "What makes you act like this?" He said: "Hardship, O Abu Lababah." Do you say that in the name of Allah?" Abu al-Yasar said: "Yes, by His name."

Then Abu Lababah said: "I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny ask: "Who likes to be sheltered from the outburst of hellfire?" We said: "All of us would like that, O messenger of Allah." He said: "Then he should give respite to his debtor - or he should redeem the financial difficulty."
